reviewPurpose: Review a newly found institutional-repository lead for inland CALABARZON fish coverage without promoting metadata-only or aggregate facts as current species observations.

source.title: Fishery resource assessment of Taal Lake, Batangas, Philippines
source.citation: Mutia, M. T. M., Muyot, M. C., Torres Jr., F. B., & Faminialagao, C. M. (2013). Fishery resource assessment of Taal Lake, Batangas, Philippines. In LakeCon2011: Building on the pillars of Integrated Lake Basin Management (pp. 217-229). PCAARRD-DOST.
source.sourceDescribedMethod: Fish landed-catch survey at major landing sites in 11 coastal towns around Taal Lake; sampling was conducted on 20 days per month during peak landing time.

accessReview.result: The repository exposes the citation, abstract and subject metadata, but reports no associated file for this item. No chapter, complete species table, underlying survey data or per-town allocation was acquired.

reuseReview.result: The repository page does not state a reuse license for the conference-paper content. Public metadata visibility is not treated as permission to extract or republish its species list.

limits: The abstract's 2010 survey summary is historical and is not a current-presence statement.
The 11 landing towns are not enumerated in the repository abstract, and named species are not allocated to individual towns or sampling sites.
The 47-species total includes non-fish organisms and cannot be represented as 47 fish species.
The record does not establish Taal Lake boundaries, municipal-water boundaries, fishing permission, legality, safety, abundance or catchability.
nextAction: If the complete chapter becomes available through ordinary authorized access, review the species table, exact landing-site scope and item-specific reuse terms; otherwise retain as a metadata-only historical lead and continue to other waterbodies.
